licence.note: Written once per process start by a bot whose pool has a labelled endpoint; the fleet (0cdb1a8) writes none (it has no such row kind).

extension.note: Primaries need ~24 h at 10 bots (design s.6 power); gates (liveness, fallback, nothing served, schema, slow, mismatch, config) are read at every read.

exposure.note: >= 6,000 gemma4 decisions AND >= 200 canary bot-hours (~20 h of 10 bots) AND every canary bot on gemma4 (G8). So no KEEP before ~20 h; the gates still REVERT at any read.

own_lines.note: G1 liveness >= 0.80 gemma4; G2 fallback <= 0.20; G3 unserved decisions <= control + 0.5/bot-h; G4 gemma4 schema-valid >= control - 0.01; G5 canary model-decision p95 <= control p95 + 15 s; G6 mismatch 0; G7 every canary bot's FIRST endpoint is gemma4; G8 every canary bot decides (>= 1 per 10 min) and >= 60% by gemma4. Deterministic mechanism checks on the canary's own rows: a failure is a defect, not a noisy estimate.
No row may claim gemma4 for a decision something else served (the proxy names lmstudio:<it> on any non-match).

primary.note: ADVISORY BY DESIGN (verdict.py: primary is advisory). A KEEP of brain-01 means: the gates held (it was live, safe, and decided by gemma4) -- NOT that it helped. promotion is 'none', so a KEEP changes nothing on the fleet; the DiDs (refused share, success share, stagnation/bot-h, stone/iron pickaxe crafts/bot-h, decisions/bot-h, items/bot-h) with their 10-12 null SDs go to the OWNER, who decides whether to keep the brain on a fixed subset (an amendment to promotion 'keep-subset', then mcai-brain-subset).

harm: The loop's death gate (two-death floor) is authoritative; brainread reports deaths/bot-h DiD.
teardown: THREE steps plus the env check: drop-ins, canary_pool, restart; then no canary bot's /proc/<pid>/environ may carry OLLAMA_BRAIN_PRIMARY (staged canary-loop.sh env-cleared check).
